args.text: [lane-stoat] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to servers that have moved or been retired, causing failures or outages. (2) Slow recovery: when a site fails over to a backup, old answers keep pointing at the broken server until the cache expires. (3) Lingering bad data: if a forged or mistaken answer is cached, it stays in place longer, so harm lasts longer.

[lane-stoat] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave you unsure whether a request worked, so you must be able to send it again. If the request is idempotent, meaning repeating it gives the same result as doing it once, a retry cannot cause harm such as a double payment or a duplicate order.

[lane-stoat] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) It leaks creation time, because the first part of the value is a timestamp, so anyone who sees an ID can tell roughly when the record was made. (2) It is larger than a plain integer key (16 bytes against 4 or 8), so indexes take more space and comparisons are a little slower, and IDs made in the same millisecond on different servers are only loosely ordered.

[lane-stoat] A write-ahead log is a file where a database records each change before it applies that change to its main data files. If the system crashes part-way through, it can replay the log on restart to recover completed work and undo unfinished work, so no data is lost or left half-written.

[lane-stoat] (1) Repeatability: a pinned client version means any change in results comes from the thing being measured, not from a client update that changes behaviour or speed. (2) Fair comparison: every run and every system under test uses the same client code, so results from different days or machines can be compared honestly and reproduced by others.

[lane-stoat] Backpressure is a way for a queue to tell the senders to slow down or stop when the receivers cannot keep up, so the queue does not grow without limit. It can work by blocking or rejecting new messages once the queue is full, which protects memory and keeps delays under control.

[lane-stoat] A cron job can run twice when (1) the same schedule is installed on two servers, or (2) a slow earlier run is still going when the next one starts. A guard is a lock, such as a lock file or database lock, that makes a new run exit at once if another is already active.

[lane-stoat] A tombstone is a small marker saved in place of a deleted item, so that every copy of the data learns the item was removed. Without it, a copy that missed the delete could send the old value back and bring the item to life again.

[lane-stoat] Two signs a test is flaky: (1) it passes and fails on the same code with no change between runs. (2) it fails only sometimes, such as under heavy load, in a different order, or at certain times, and passes when run again.

[lane-stoat] A lease lock gives a holder the lock for a set time. Clock skew means two machines disagree about the time. So the holder may think it still has the lock after the lock service has expired it and given it to another, and both then act at once.
